title: Chronicles of the Black Company (Chronicles of the Black Company Series Book 1)
author: Glen Cook

highlights.text: When I reflect on my companions’ inner natures I usually wish I controlled one small talent. I wish I could look inside them and unmask the darks and brights that move them. Then I take a quick look into the jungle of my own soul and thank heaven that I cannot. Any man who barely sustains an armistice with himself has no business poking around in an alien soul.

There are no self-proclaimed villains, only regiments of self-proclaimed saints. Victorious historians rule where good or evil lies. We abjure labels. We fight for money and an indefinable pride. The politics, the ethics, the moralities, are irrelevant.

You who come after me, scribbling these Annals, by now realize that I shy off portraying the whole truth about our band of blackguards. You know they are vicious, violent, and ignorant. They are complete barbarians, living out their cruelest fantasies, their behavior tempered only by the presence of a few decent men. I do not often show that side because these men are my brethren, my family, and I was taught young not to speak ill of kin. The old lessons die hardest.

I am a haunted man. I am haunted by the Limper’s screams. I am haunted by the Lady’s laughter. I am haunted by my suspicion that we are furthering the cause of something that deserves to be scrubbed from the face of the earth. I am haunted by the conviction that those bent upon the Lady’s eradication are little better than she. I am haunted by the clear knowledge that, in the end, evil always triumphs.
“Evil is relative, Annalist. You can’t hang a sign on it. You can’t touch it or taste it or cut it with a sword. Evil depends on where you are standing, pointing your indicting finger.

I did not believe in evil as an active force, only as a matter of viewpoint, yet I had seen enough to make me question my philosophy. If the Lady were not evil incarnate, then she was as close as made no difference.
There are the physically dead and the morally dead. My comrades were among the latter.
And yet, could I condemn them? They were my brothers, my friends, my family, and acted moral within that context. The weight of it fell on me. I had to convince them there was a larger obligation.
Characters like me don’t become prophets. Especially not from the wrong side.

Back to the Company. Back to business. Back to the parade of years. Back to these Annals. Back to fear. Thirty-seven years before the comet returns. The vision has to be false. I’ll never survive that long. Will I?

All men are born condemned, so the wise say. All suckle the breast of Death. All bow before that Silent Monarch. That Lord in Shadow lifts a finger. A feather flutters to the earth. There is no reason in His song. The good go young. The wicked prosper. He is king of the Chaos Lords. His breath stills all souls.
You try your damnedest, but something always goes wrong. That’s life. If you’re smart, you plan for it.
“It’s not the morality, Croaker. What’s moral in war? Superior strength. No. I’m just tired.” “Not an adventure anymore, eh?” “Stopped being that a long time ago. Turned into a job.

There’s always another province, always more Rebels. They breed like maggots in a cowpie. I’m getting older and older, and I haven’t done anything to make a better world. In fact, if you backed off to look at it, we’ve all made it worse.”
One did not question money’s provenance. It had no memory.
He almost wept as he tramped homeward. It never got any better. He was always in a trap.
It is a hostile, bitter land where none of the normal rules apply. Rocks speak and whales fly. Coral grows in the desert. Trees walk. And the inhabitants are the strangest of all.
We are the victims of our own competence. She always wants us where the going threatens to become toughest. She knows we will do the best job. Damn and double damn.
“Your nerves aren’t my problem, Shed. They’re yours. You lost them. Only you can find them again.”
“You always do what a coward would. Which is why I don’t trust you. Anybody can scare you. And you had all that money.
Right now you’re acting more like Marron Shed than like Raven. Old Shed is the guy who panics. Remember?”
“What’re Taken?” Shed asked. “If you have gods, Shed, pray that you never find out. Pray hard.”
“Think about it anyway, Shed. I know what I’m talking about. I used to work for those people.”
There wasn’t much justice in the Buskin, but what there was was quick and rough. They would hang him sure.
So. As always, the shit rolls downhill. The normal course would be for me to go out and tromp on somebody below me.
“You should have seen that Shed,” Pawnbroker cackled. “A chicken sweating like a pig and lying like a dog. A one-man barnyard.”
Sometimes lust pulled ahead, sometimes the urge toward responsibility. He ached for Sue.… He should not need money if she really loved him.…
There is no vengeance as terrible as the vengeance a coward plots in the dark of his heart.
“Sue, I loved you. I really did. I would have done anything for you. When you kill a love like that, you turn it into a big hatred.”
“How can anybody so young be so heartless?” “You don’t prosper in the Buskin if you have a heart, Mr. Shed.
“Bring us more live ones, Marron Shed. We have many uses for live ones.”

I do not think I have met many men who disgusted me more. Nastier men, yes. I have encountered scores. Greater villains come by the battalion. Shed’s leavening of self-pity and cowardice reduced him from those categories to an essentially pathetic level.

He had a hidden streak of charity and decency. It was the gradual growth of that spark, with its eventual impact upon the Black Company, which makes me feel obligated to record all the earlier noxious details about that frightened little man.
The world knows where it stands with the Lady. It is the Rebel whose ideals and morals conflict with fact, becoming as changeable as the weather and as flexible as a snake.
He had known they were hard men, men who did not play games. He had not realized just how hard they were, how savage they could be.
I have been told I always look at the dark underbelly of tomorrow. Possibly. You’re less likely to be disappointed that way.
We’re the Black Company. We’re not good or evil. We’re just soldiers with swords for sale. But I’m tired of having our work turned to wicked ends.

You mess with people’s religion and you mess with fire. Even people who don’t much give a damn. Religion is something that gets hammered in early, and never really goes away. And has powers to move which go beyond anything rational.
“Raven. I hated you. But I loved you, too. You were the worst villain I ever knew. And as good a friend as I ever had. You made me start thinking like a man.”
“I didn’t say I didn’t want to do something. I said I can’t. You don’t ask a man with a penknife to chop down a forest and build a city. He doesn’t have the tools.”
“Can’t take them with us, Croaker.” “I know.” He swung around, started back. Alone. Not even Otto joined him, and Otto has very little conscience.
“Got to find out what happened,” One-Eye said. He muttered, “If that bastard Goblin got himself killed, I’ll wring his neck.”
